_meta.purpose: Per-jurisdiction verification manifest. Maps every encoded statutory parameter to the primary source and agency page a reviewer checks it against, plus the structural claims (eligibility logic, formulas, job-protection rules) that are not single numbers.
_meta.disclaimer: Every value in this repo is web-researched and UNVERIFIED by counsel. `verified: false` on a jurisdiction means no employment lawyer has signed off yet. This manifest is the worksheet for that review, not evidence it has happened.
_meta.how_to_use: A reviewer works one jurisdiction at a time: open the source pages, check each parameter's value(s) and effective date(s) against the agency's published figures and the cited statute, check each structural claim, then set verified/verified_by/verified_on. Run `python -m openleave.references check` to confirm the manifest still covers every encoded parameter.

FMLA.program: Federal Family and Medical Leave Act

parameters.fmla.min_hours: Hours worked in prior 12 months to qualify
parameters.fmla.min_worksite_headcount: Employees within 75 miles for employer coverage

claims: Employee must have worked 12 months for the employer (need not be consecutive).
Leave is unpaid and job-protected; runs concurrently with state paid leave for the same reason.

CA.program: California Paid Family Leave (PFL) and CFRA
CA.statute: Cal. Unemp. Ins. Code §§ 3300-3306 (PFL); Cal. Gov. Code § 12945.2 (CFRA)

parameters.ca.saww: State average weekly wage used in the PFL benefit tiers ($)
parameters.ca.pfl.low_earner_rate: Wage-replacement rate below the SAWW breakpoint (fraction)
parameters.ca.pfl.standard_rate: Wage-replacement rate above the SAWW breakpoint (fraction)

claims: PFL provides wage replacement only; CFRA supplies the job protection (5+ employees).
The 2025 rate change raised the low-earner rate to 90% and standard rate to 70%.

CO.program: Colorado Family and Medical Leave Insurance (FAMLI)

parameters.co.min_base_period_earnings: Minimum wages earned in Colorado to qualify ($)
parameters.co.combined.weeks: Maximum combined weeks including the pregnancy addition
parameters.co.job_protection.min_service_days: Days of service for job protection

claims: Eligibility is a $-earned floor across any employer, not an hours or tenure test.
Job protection has NO employer-size threshold (unlike FMLA).
Max weekly benefit changed mid-year on 2026-07-01 ($1,381.45 -> $1,448.02).

CT.program: Connecticut Paid Leave, with CT FMLA job protection
CT.statute: Conn. Gen. Stat. § 31-49e et seq. (paid leave); § 31-51kk et seq. (CT FMLA)

parameters.ct.minimum_wage: State minimum wage; the whole benefit schedule is pegged to it ($/hr)
parameters.ct.pfml.cap_hours: Cap as a multiple of the hourly minimum wage (hours)
parameters.ct.pfml.tier_break_hours: Tier breakpoint as a multiple of the hourly minimum wage (hours)
parameters.ct.fmla.min_tenure_months: Months of service for CT FMLA job protection

claims: Cap = 60x and breakpoint = 40x the hourly minimum wage; both move when the wage moves.
Job protection is the SEPARATE CT FMLA, which reaches employers with a single employee.

DC.program: DC Paid Family Leave, with DC FMLA job protection
DC.statute: D.C. Code § 32-541.01 et seq. (paid leave); § 32-501 et seq. (DC FMLA)

parameters.dc.minimum_wage: DC minimum wage; the benefit threshold is pegged to it ($/hr)
parameters.dc.pfl.max_weekly_benefit: Maximum weekly benefit set by DOES ($)
parameters.dc.pfl.threshold_multiple: Tier-1 ceiling as a multiple of (min wage x 40 hrs)
parameters.dc.fmla.min_employees: Employer-size threshold for DC FMLA job protection
parameters.dc.fmla.min_tenure_months: Months of service for DC FMLA job protection
parameters.dc.fmla.min_hours: Hours in prior year for DC FMLA job protection

claims: DC PFL has NO earnings, hours, or tenure minimum for benefits.
Job protection is the NARROWER DC FMLA (20+ employees), so DC pays more workers than it protects.
DC minimum wage rises $17.95 -> $18.40 on 2026-07-01, widening the 90% band.
Max weekly benefit is $1,190 for leave dates on or after 2025-09-28.

DE.program: Delaware Paid Leave (Healthy Delaware Families Act)

parameters.de.combined.weeks: Maximum combined weeks per application year
parameters.de.parental.min_employees: Employer size to owe parental leave
parameters.de.medical_family.min_employees: Employer size to owe medical/family leave
parameters.de.eligibility.min_hours: Hours in prior 12 months to qualify

claims: Coverage depends on employer size AND reason: <10 not covered, 10-24 parental-only, 25+ all reasons.
Benefits began 2026-01-01; max $900 / min $100 is fixed for 2026 and 2027.
Delaware provides job restoration to eligible employees.

MA.program: Massachusetts Paid Family and Medical Leave (PFML)

parameters.ma.combined.weeks: Maximum combined weeks per benefit year

claims: Two-tier benefit (80% then 50%) capped at 64% of SAWW.
Eligibility includes a self-referential 30x-weekly-benefit earnings test.
Job protection is built into c. 175M itself; no companion statute needed.
7-day unpaid waiting period at the start of leave.

MD.program: Maryland FAMLI (Time to Care Act) - NOT YET IN FORCE
MD.statute: Md. Code, Lab. & Empl. § 8.3-101 et seq.

parameters.md.eligibility.min_hours: Hours worked in Maryland in prior 4 quarters to qualify
parameters.md.extended.weeks: Maximum weeks when combining bonding + own serious health condition

claims: Benefits are NOT payable until 2028-01-03 (HB 102, 2025); contributions begin 2027-01-01.
The launch-year SAWW is set annually by the Secretary of Labor and is not yet published.
This encoding returns weekly_benefit=None on/after the in-force date rather than a fabricated figure.

ME.program: Maine Paid Family and Medical Leave (PFML)

parameters.me.saww: State average weekly wage; also the benefit cap ($)
parameters.me.tier_threshold_fraction: Breakpoint as a fraction of the SAWW
parameters.me.eligibility_saww_multiple: Base-period earnings floor as a multiple of the SAWW
parameters.me.combined.weeks: Maximum combined weeks per benefit year
parameters.me.job_protection.min_service_days: Days of service for job protection

claims: Second tier is 66% (not the usual 50%), capped at 100% of the SAWW.
Benefits began 2026-05-01; the SAWW/cap rose $1,198 -> $1,249.12 on 2026-07-01.
Eligibility is 6x the SAWW earned in the base period.

parameters.mn.wage_threshold_fraction_of_saww: Earnings floor as a fraction of the SAWW
parameters.mn.combined.weeks: Maximum combined weeks per benefit year

claims: Benefits begin 2026-01-01; paid and job-protected after 90 days.
The earnings floor is 5.3% of the SAWW (annualized): verify the threshold fraction and that it is applied to 52x the weekly wage.

NJ.program: New Jersey Family Leave Insurance (FLI), with NJFLA job protection
NJ.statute: N.J.S.A. 43:21-25 et seq. (FLI); N.J.S.A. 34:11B-1 et seq. (NJFLA)

parameters.nj.fli.base_week_earnings: Weekly earnings that count as a 'base week' ($)
parameters.nj.njfla.min_employees: Employer size for NJFLA job protection
parameters.nj.njfla.min_hours: Hours in prior 12 months for NJFLA job protection

claims: FLI pays 85% but historically carried no job protection of its own.
A3451 adds FLI reinstatement from 2026-07-17; before that, protection is NJFLA-only.
NJFLA thresholds (30 employees, 1,000 hours) are strictly easier than FMLA's, so FMLA is never NJ FLI's sole fallback protector.
Low earners meeting only the 20-base-week alternative return eligible=null (needs week-level data).
Benefit is 67% of the employee's average weekly wage, capped at 67% of the SAWW.
PFL is job-protected.

parameters.or.combined.weeks: Maximum combined weeks per benefit year
parameters.or.job_protection.min_service_days: Days of service for job restoration

claims: Low earners (<= 65% of SAWW) are replaced at 100% of wages, then 50% above.
Job restoration applies at EVERY employer size (the 25-employee line is about premiums).
Benefit-year figures update ~late June; $1,692.16 cap applies from 2026-06-28.

RI.program: Rhode Island Temporary Disability (TDI) + Temporary Caregiver (TCI) Insurance

parameters.ri.benefit_rate_of_high_quarter: Weekly benefit as a fraction of highest base-period quarter
parameters.ri.aww_cap_fraction: Benefit ceiling as a fraction of the average weekly wage
parameters.ri.max_weekly_benefit: Maximum weekly benefit before dependency allowance ($)
parameters.ri.min_base_period_earnings: Base-period earnings for the primary eligibility test ($)

claims: Benefit is 4.62% of the highest base-period quarter, not to exceed 85% of the AWW.
TCI (bonding/family) is job-protected; TDI (own disability) is not.
Military-exigency leave is not a covered reason.
A dependency allowance (up to $1,552 with five dependents) is NOT modeled by the engine.
Max $1,150 / min $148 effective 2026-07-01.

WA.program: Washington Paid Family and Medical Leave (PFML)

parameters.wa.min_hours: Hours in the qualifying period to be benefit-eligible
parameters.wa.combined.weeks: Maximum combined weeks per claim year
parameters.wa.job_protection.min_service_days: Days of service for job protection (from 2026)

claims: Eligibility is 820 hours across ANY Washington employer, not tenure with the current one.
Job protection is a separate test that expanded on 2026-01-01 (50->25 employees, 12mo->180 days, 1,250-hr rule removed).
Two-tier benefit: 90% up to 50% of SAWW, then 50%.

FED-WAGE.program: Federal wage & hour (FLSA) — minimum wage and tip credit
claims: Federal minimum wage has been $7.25 since 2009-07-24.
Tipped cash wage $2.13 + max tip credit $5.12 = the $7.25 floor; tips must make up the difference.
State minimum wages and state tip-credit rules override this floor where higher/stricter.

CA-WAGE.program: California wage & hour — minimum wage and final pay

parameters.minwage.CA: California state minimum wage, all employers ($/hr)
parameters.finalpay.CA.quit_no_notice_hours: Deadline to pay a no-notice quit (hours)

claims: Minimum wage is CPI-indexed annually: $16.50 (2025) -> $16.90 (2026), all employer sizes.
California prohibits the tip credit (Lab. Code § 351): tipped workers get full minimum in cash.
Fired/laid off -> pay immediately; quit with 72h notice -> last day; quit without -> within 72h.
Accrued vacation is earned wages and must be paid out (§ 227.3).
The finalpay.* effective dates are 'in force since at least 2000' floors, not researched precisely.

WA-WAGE.program: Washington wage & hour — minimum wage and final pay
claims: Minimum wage is CPI-indexed annually: $16.66 (2025) -> $17.13 (2026), highest state rate in the nation.
Washington prohibits the tip credit: tipped workers get full minimum in cash.
Final wages are due by the end of the next established pay period; no statutory vacation payout.
Many WA localities (Seattle $21.30 in 2026, SeaTac, Tukwila, etc.) set higher minimums — not encoded.
